:::{#thm-solution-set}
#### All solutions of a linear system

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$ with a generalized inverse $\matr{G}$ (@def-generalized-inverse).

1. $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A}) = \mathcal{C}(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})$:
   $\vecf{x}$ solves $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$
   exactly when $\vecf{x} = (\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{q}$ for some $\vecf{q} \in \reals^n$.
2. If $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ is consistent (@thm-consistency),
   then $\vecf{x}$ is a solution exactly when
   $$
   \vecf{x} = \matr{G} \vecf{b} + (\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{q}
   \quad \text{for some } \vecf{q} \in \reals^n:
   $$
   one particular solution plus a vector of $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
First,

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})
&= \matr{A} \matr{I}_n - \matr{A} \matr{G} \matr{A}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib, and } \matr{A}\,(-\matr{M}) = -\matr{A} \matr{M} \text{ by @def-scalar-mult)}
\\
&= \matr{A} - \matr{A} \matr{G} \matr{A}
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\\
&= \matr{A} - \matr{A}
&& \text{(@def-generalized-inverse)}
\\
&= \matr{0}_{m \times n},
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{A}\,(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{q} = \vzero_m$ for every $\vecf{q}$
(@thm-matmul-assoc),
and $\mathcal{C}(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A}) \subseteq \mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$.
Conversely, if $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$, then

$$
\ba
(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{x}
&= \matr{I}_n \vecf{x} - (\matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{x}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib, and @def-scalar-mult)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} - (\matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{x}
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} - \matr{G}\,(\matr{A} \vecf{x})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} - \matr{G}\,\vzero_m
&& \text{(} \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m \text{)}
\\
&= \vecf{x},
&& \text{(} \matr{G}\,\vzero_m = \vzero_n \text{)}
\ea
$$

so $\vecf{x}$ is in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})$, with $\vecf{q} = \vecf{x}$.

**Part 2.**
$\matr{G} \vecf{b}$ is a solution (@thm-generalized-inverse-solves).
For any $\vecf{x}$,

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(\vecf{x} - \matr{G} \vecf{b})
&= \matr{A} \vecf{x} - \matr{A}\,(\matr{G} \vecf{b})
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-linear, with coefficients } 1 \text{ and } -1 \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{A} \vecf{x} - \matr{A} \matr{G} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{A} \vecf{x} - \vecf{b},
&& \text{(@thm-consistency, statement 3)}
\ea
$$

so $\vecf{x}$ solves $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$
exactly when $\vecf{x} - \matr{G} \vecf{b} \in \mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$,
that is, by part 1, exactly when
$\vecf{x} - \matr{G} \vecf{b} = (\matr{I}_n - \matr{G} \matr{A})\,\vecf{q}$ for some $\vecf{q}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-solution-set}
#### All solutions of a consistent system

For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\matr{G} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\vecf{b} = (2, 0)$:
$\matr{G} \vecf{b} = (2, 14)$, $\matr{G} \matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
and $\matr{I}_2 - \matr{G} \matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ -7 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
so

$$
\vecf{x} = (2, 14) + (0, -7 q_1 + q_2), \qquad q_1, q_2 \in \reals.
$$

Since $-7 q_1 + q_2$ can be any number,
the solutions are exactly the vectors $(2, t)$, $t \in \reals$,
which is what $\matr{A}\,(x_1, x_2) = (x_1, 0) = (2, 0)$ says directly.

:::
